name: Mehetabel
overview: Mehetabel is a male biblical figure identified primarily as the father of Delaiah, as recorded in Nehemiah 6:10. There is no tribal affiliation or additional notes provided about him, making his identity largely defined by this paternal relationship.
namesAndTitles: The name Mehetabel means 'G-d [El] does good,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning common in Hebrew names. This proper name is not indicated to have been given directly by God, but it emphasizes divine goodness as part of his identity.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Mehetabel as the father of Delaiah, specifically referenced in Nehemiah 6:10. Beyond this paternal link, no other family relationships are documented for him in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Mehetabel's significance in the biblical narrative is tied to his mention as the father of Delaiah, situating him within the post-exilic community described in Nehemiah. His name's meaning underscores a recognition of God's goodness amidst the restoration period. While not a central figure, his inclusion in the genealogical records supports the historical and spiritual continuity of God's people.
